title: Sort Array By Parity
statement: Rearrange the integers of `nums` so that every even value sits before every odd value, and return the rearranged array (changing `nums` in place and returning it is fine). The relative order inside the even group and inside the odd group does not matter: any arrangement that keeps all evens ahead of all odds is accepted.
notes:
## Intuition

The simplest idea is to build two lists, the even values and the odd values, and join them; that uses O(n) extra space. Since the order inside each group does not matter, we can instead fix the array in place: an odd value near the front and an even value near the back are both in the wrong half, and one swap repairs both at once.

## Approach

1. Put `left` at the first index and `right` at the last.
2. While `left < right`: if `nums[left]` is even it is already in place, so move `left` forward.
3. Otherwise, if `nums[right]` is odd it is already in place, so move `right` back.
4. Otherwise `nums[left]` is odd and `nums[right]` is even: swap them and move both pointers inward.
5. Return `nums`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, 1, 2, 4]`, `left = 0`, `right = 3`. `3` is odd and `4` is even, so they swap: `[4, 1, 2, 3]`, `left = 1`, `right = 2`. `1` is odd and `2` is even, so they swap: `[4, 2, 1, 3]`, `left = 2`, `right = 1`. The pointers have crossed, so the answer is `[4, 2, 1, 3]`, one of the accepted orders.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): every step moves at least one pointer inward.
- Space: O(1): the swaps happen inside `nums`.

## Pitfalls

- Use `left < right`, not `<=`; a single middle value is already correct.
- Test parity with `% 2`; `0` counts as even.
- After a swap, move both pointers, or the loop re-checks values it just fixed.
- The expected output is not unique, so do not try to match one specific order.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left` | first index not yet known to hold an even value |
| `right` | last index not yet known to hold an odd value |

narration.2: Start the left pointer at the front of the array.
narration.3: Start the right pointer at the back.
narration.4: Keep working until the two pointers meet.
narration.5: An even value at the front is already where it belongs.
narration.7: An odd value at the back is already where it belongs.
narration.10: Here left holds an odd value and right holds an even one: swap them.
narration.11: The front slot is now even, so step left forward...
narration.12: ...and the back slot is now odd, so step right back.
narration.15: Every even value is now ahead of every odd one; return the array.
